title: CashGuard spending priors (backend/data/priors.json)
description: Single-adult priors for VARIABLE spending, read by E6 (baselines, arch 5.3.5) and E8 (short-history forecast). Fixed costs (housing_rent, utilities, telecom, subscriptions) have no prior: they come from each person's fixed costs and recurring detection (David G., D-variable). E6: for the household-scaled categories of app.domain.enums.HOUSEHOLD_SCALED_CATEGORIES the prior is x household_scale x city_index, except kids, which is PER CHILD: x number of children (0 children -> 0) x city_index (D-kids); every other category uses the plain prior. Blend with the person's history: (n*personal + 5*prior)/(n + 5). All values are fictional, in RON, at Bucharest prices. Load it strictly: numbers as Decimal, duplicate keys and NaN / Infinity rejected, as tests/unit/datafiles.py parse_json does.

categories.description: Every variable spending category of arch 4.5: not transfers, income, savings (not spending) and not the fixed costs.

cities.description: City indices (arch 5.3.5). A user's city matches a city when key(city) equals key(one of its names), key = app.i18n.text.fold, every run of non-letters/digits as a separator, the city_ignored_words and pure numbers dropped, the remaining words joined without spaces ('Municipiul Bucuresti, Sector 3' -> 'bucuresti', 'Cluj Napoca' -> 'clujnapoca').

city_ignored_words.description: Folded words dropped by the city key: administrative prefixes, the country, Bucharest's sectors.

default_city_index.description: The index of a city that isn't listed (E6: unknown city -> 1.0).

monthly_mean.description: A single adult's MEAN monthly spending in this category, RON (kids: per child). A mean, not a median: for lumpy categories the median month is about 0. E6 monthly_expected; E8 lognormal by its mean.

basket_median.description: A single adult's median single transaction in this category, RON (E6 prior_median).

basket_cv.description: The spread of one transaction's amount (lognormal coefficient of variation).

cv.description: Coefficient of variation of the MONTHLY total under a compound Poisson model: purchases at rate monthly_mean / (basket_median * sqrt(1 + basket_cv^2)), each a lognormal amount; cv = sqrt((1 + basket_cv^2)^1.5 * basket_median / monthly_mean). Lumpy categories (a basket above the month) reach ~3.5, hence the cap of 5 (the spec's 2 was too low). For E8 (arch 6.7 uses a flat 0.25; danutu decides). Seasonal for E8: gifts (December, March, Easter), travel (summer), kids (school start, 1 June, December), clothing (season changes); dates in data/calendar.json.
